title: Enumeration reducibility and positive information

based_on.title: Computable Structure Theory: Within the arithmetic
based_on.pages: Part1 draft compiled June25,2019; Notation and Conventions, printed p.xvii (PDF17): operator definition and total-information embedding statement; elementary proofs supplied here

summary: Compute sets from finite positive witnesses, compose the rules uniformly, and recover Turing degrees by tagging both oracle answers.
abstract: Seeing a number enter a set provides positive evidence; waiting for a number that has not appeared does not certify its absence. Enumeration reducibility formalizes computations that produce a set using only finite collections of positive observations from another set. These rules compose through an explicit uniform construction, and their degrees have tagged joins and a least degree containing every computably enumerable set. Membership oracles supply more information because they also answer no. Recording each yes or no answer as a different positive tag makes that distinction precise: the resulting total-information sets embed Turing degrees into enumeration degrees, preserving and reflecting their order.
